text: Python classes support three kinds of methods, each with a different job.
The most common is the instance method — it takes self and works with a specific object's data.
area uses self dot radius to compute the area for this particular circle.
[chuckle] A class method takes cls instead of self, and works with the class as a whole.
It's perfect as a factory — here unit builds and returns a ready-made circle of radius one.
[sniff] A static method takes neither self nor cls — it's just a plain function living inside the class.
Use it for helper logic that belongs with the class but doesn't need any object or class data.
describe simply returns a description, needing nothing from any instance.
[groan] Instance methods for object data, class methods for factories, static methods for related helpers — that's the trio.
